newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM targets broader sales spread.
newsitem.headline: DSM targets broader sales spread.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM said on Tuesday it was targeting a broader spread of sales over the various geographical regions in a bid to reduce its cyclical exposure.

"We are aiming for a greater spread of our turnover over the various regions. At the beginning of the next century round 20 percent of group turnover should come from North America and 20 percent from Asia," DSM chairman Simon de Bree told a news conference on the company's 1996 results.
"Implementing this strategy will also (mean)...that our financial results will gradually fluctuate less," De Bree said.
Currently DSM derives some 71 percent of group turnover in Europe, compared with 15.7 percent in North America and 13-14 percent in Asia, finance director Louk Ligthart said.
Broadly speaking, DSM group turnover was expected to grow to some 15 billion guilders by 2000, De Bree said.
But he he noted this was strongly dependent on currency fluctuations and often volatile pricing.
DSM posted 1996 net sales of 10.26 billion guilders, up from 9.82 billion guilders in 1995.
DSM would also continue its diversification into less cyclical sectors such as fine chemicals, he added.
